text:
incident-bot: Pager: INC-2026-0409 billing: token count drift detected across ingestion pipeline (alerts from metering-alerts). Priority: P1. Affected: customer-facing overage flags, delayed daily usage exports.

marta: paging in — saw alerts for multiple customers showing sudden spike in token counts then dropoffs. overage flags are noisy.

aj: jumping in. which pipeline? ingest-stream or batch-recon?

marta: looks like realtime ingest path (kinesis -> token-counter service). batch-recon still shows expected counts but delayed by ~2h. top symptoms: deltas between realtime metrics and batch snapshots.

billing-eng: we got customer reports of overage emails. can you confirm which customers? I have a few on the message thread.

emily-cs: customers: acme-inc, beta-saas, and a handful of enterprise tenants reported overages. they say usage shows huge spikes between 01:10-01:30 UTC then nothing.

oncall-sre: reproducing locally — tailing token-counter logs. attaching snippets.

oncall-sre: ```
2026-04-09T01:12:03Z token-counter[pid=88] INFO emit count=0 window_id=2026-04-09T01:12
2026-04-09T01:12:04Z token-counter[pid=88] WARN publish failed: timeout to metering-emit (503)
2026-04-09T01:12:05Z token-counter[pid=88] INFO buffered tokens=19234
2026-04-09T01:12:07Z token-counter[pid=88] INFO emit succeeded count=19234
```

marta: interesting — looks like transient 503s to metering-emit causing buffers to backlog. but why do overage flags show spikes? maybe double-counting on retry path.

billing-eng: we have a retry-loop that can duplicate if ack not persisted before retry. last code change to token-counter was a month ago (idempotency header added but not uniformly).

aj: reading the code: retry path doesn't attach idempotency-key when backing off to the fallback emitter. iirc fallback is async and doesn't dedupe.

lucas: confirming: fallback-emitter uses redis queue + worker that doesn't check request-id. that can cause duplicates on retries if both primary and fallback succeed.

emily-cs: customers are seeing billing UI show an enormous spike, then later corrected. they want timelines to respond.

marta: mitigation plan: 1) pause sending automated overage emails (billing-eng approved), 2) enable a temporary circuit-breaker to stop fallback-emitter from dequeuing until we validate dedupe, 3) backfill reconciliation to correct counts before billing jobs run.

billing-eng: pausing email notifications now — toggled feature flag: billing.send_overage_emails=false :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: applying circuit-breaker: scaling the fallback-emitter to 0 replicas in staging then prod. running `kubectl scale deploy/fallback-emitter --replicas=0 -n metering`.

oncall-sre: ```
$ kubectl scale deploy/fallback-emitter --replicas=0 -n metering
deployment.apps/fallback-emitter scaled
```

aj: while fallback is disabled, we need to drain the redis queue to avoid data loss: move messages to a staging queue for manual dedupe. running small script to pop and tag with request-id where present.

aj: ```python
# quick pop script
import redis
r = redis.from_url("redis://metering-redis:6379/0")
for _ in range(10000):
    item = r.lpop('fallback:queue')
    if not item: break
    # parse and write to fallback:staging for manual dedupe
    r.rpush('fallback:staging', item)
```

marta: good. billing-eng, can you confirm backfill window and priority for recon job? we want to ensure invoices aren't generated with bad counts.

billing-eng: backfill job created as high-priority: run-recon --since 2026-04-09T00:00 --until 2026-04-09T02:00 --dry-run then promote. target: complete within 3 hours.

emily-cs: CS team will hold any billing communications until recon finishes and we have corrected deltas. please provide ETA updates every 30m.

oncall-sre: initial metrics: backlog peaked at ~140k buffered tokens across token-counter instances. emit success rate recovered at 01:15 UTC when metering-emit returned 200s. suspected root cause: upstream transient 503s from metering-emit combined with non-idempotent fallback.

marta: ask: any customer-visible throttling? we should check API latency alerts.

oncall-sre: API latency fine. only billing pipeline affected. no customer request errors reported in prod API.

aj: I've instrumented an adhoc dedupe run on 2500 messages in fallback:staging, found ~320 duplicates. seems consistent with double-emits during the outage window.

billing-eng: plan to correct counts: reconcile primary emitted counts vs fallback deduped counts; apply deltas to billing ledger; mark invoices in the window as pending. we'll run dry-run first and post diff.

marta: action items (assigned):
- billing-eng: run dry-run recon and post diff to thread (ETA 01:50 UTC)
- aj: continue draining fallback queue to staging and run dedupe script (ongoing)
- oncall-sre: keep fallback-emitter scaled to 0 until we confirm idempotency fix deployed (ongoing)
- emily-cs: hold communications and prepare customer-facing timeline once we have reconciled numbers (ongoing)

lucas: started a branch to add request-id propagation to fallback-emitter + idempotency check in worker. will aim for canary in 2h.

marta: customer impact assessment (initial): potential incorrect temporary overage emails to ~12 customers, no charge applied yet, invoices not finalized. severity: medium but could escalate if not reconciled before billing run.

emily-cs: noted — prepping customer messages that say we detected a metering glitch and are reconciling counts. will wait for final numbers.

incident-bot: Update: Pager status set to acknowledged by marta at 2026-04-09T01:34:20Z.

oncall-sre: recon dry-run completed. attached summary: total_delta = -35,420 tokens across affected tenants (i.e., duplicates to be removed).

billing-eng: applying corrections now (dry-run approved). running `run-recon --apply --window 2026-04-09T00:00,2026-04-09T02:00`.

billing-eng: corrections applied. invoice generation deferred. will re-run nightly bill generation after validations.

emily-cs: drafted customer note, waiting on final confirmation that corrections are persisted.

marta: re-enable fallback-emitter only after idempotency merged and canary verified. lucas: ping when canary ready.

lucas: canary deployed to staging at 03:10 UTC, no duplicates observed for 45m. scheduling prod canary at 04:00 UTC low-traffic window.

marta: final postmortem items: root cause = transient 503s + non-idempotent fallback leading to duplicate emits; mitigations = feature-flag for overage emails, circuit-breaker for fallback-emitter, dedupe/backfill & idempotency fix; follow-ups: add integration tests for emitter retries and idempotency, add alert to detect emit duplication rate.

emily-cs: CS will send templated message to affected customers once billing-eng confirms no outstanding deltas.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0409 transitioned to resolved at 2026-04-09T05:20:01Z (duration ~3h45m).
